---
name: grok-bot-backup-getting-started
description: >-
  Use when the Grok Bot Backup bot is first imported, or the owner asks how to
  set up their Grok Bot backup. Walks them through setup one question at a time.
---
# Getting started

Talk to the new owner directly, in first person. Open with one line: "I back up your Grok Bots' instructions, routines, skills and (if you want) memory to a private git repo every night, and I only speak up if something breaks."

## Ask, one question at a time

Wait for each answer before the next. Keep each question short and offer the default.
1. Where should the backup live? GitHub (default), GitLab or another git host?
2. What should the repo be called? Suggest `grok-bot-backup`.
3. Which bots should I include? List the bots found under `/home/box/agent-data/agents/` by name. Default: all.
4. Should I include memory? Explain plainly that memory holds personal details (family, health, money, schedules), so the repo must stay private. Default: yes, if they're comfortable with a private repo.
5. What time should it run each night? Default 2:30 AM their time.

## Then do this (follow the back-up-grok-bots-to-git skill)

1. Build the snapshot locally with their choices and tell them how many bots, routines and skills it captured and that the secret scan came back clean.
2. Ask them to create an empty private repo with that name (no README) and send the HTTPS link.
3. Ask for a repo-only token (on GitHub, a fine-grained token limited to that repo with Contents read and write, ~90-day expiry). Collect it with a masked secret request, never in chat, and ask the expiry date.
4. Add the remote, run the snapshot and push. Confirm the commit is there and the repo is private.
5. Create the nightly routine at their time (it exports live routines and memory first, then runs the snapshot; silent on success, one report on failure) and a one-time reminder 7 days before the token expires.
6. Wrap up in two or three lines: where the backup lives, when it runs, when the token reminder fires, and that they'll only hear from me if something breaks.

Don't make the repo public, don't add collaborators, and don't send or post anything on their behalf as part of setup.

---
name: back-up-grok-bots-to-git
description: >-
  Use when the owner wants their Grok Bots' definitions (instructions, settings,
  routines, skills, memory, connector instructions) backed up to a private git
  repo nightly, wants that backup set up or repaired, or needs the push token
  rotated.
---
# Back up Grok Bots to a private git repo

Goal: a private repo that can rebuild every bot's *definition* — who it is, how it is
configured, what it remembers, and what runs on a schedule — refreshed nightly, quiet on
success, loud exactly once on failure. Data, secrets, and history stay out.

## 1. What goes in, what stays out

Discover everything from the box; never hardcode agent ids.
- Bots: `ls /home/box/agent-data/agents/` — each folder with a `profile.json` is a bot. Read
  `.name` from `profile.json` to label it and use a slug of the name as the folder in the repo.

**Back up (per bot, under `agents/<slug>/`):**
- `profile.json` (name + instructions/persona), `settings.json`, `group.json`, `projects.json`
- any persona/instruction markdown files at the bot root
- live routines and memory exported by the nightly routine (see "Live routines and memory")
- legacy `memory/**/*.md` and `automations/<routine>/automation.json` box files, filed under `legacy-files/`

**Back up (shared):**
- `/home/box/agent-data/user-memory/**/*.md` → `user-memory/` (opt-in, same as memory)
- user-created skills in `/home/box/agent-data/workflows/` → `skills/`
- connector custom instructions only: the `mcpCustomInstructions`,
  `mcpCustomInstructionsByServerId`, and `autoReviewInstructions` keys from
  `/home/box/agent-data/settings.json` → `connectors/custom-instructions.json`. Nothing else
  from that file (it holds account scopes and machine ids).

**Never back up:**
- Secrets of any kind: `*secret*`, `*token*`, `*credential*`, `.env*`, keys/certs
  (`*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `id_ed25519*`), gateway/host/box secret JSON files, `.netrc`,
  `.git-credentials`.
- Browser profiles and cookies (including cookie seed files).
- Chat databases (`*.db`, `*.sqlite*`, search index), transcripts (`agent-transcripts/`,
  `*.jsonl`), audit logs, routine run histories (`runs.json`), voice-call records.
- Attachments, assets, avatars, and working files (PDFs, exports, notes the bot made) —
  those are data, not definitions.
- Built-in managed skills and plugin skills (they ship with Grok Bot).
- `node_modules/`, virtualenvs, `__pycache__/`, anything over 5 MB.

## 2. Privacy warning — say this before building

Memory files routinely contain personal details: family, health, money, addresses,
schedules. If memory is included the repo **must be private**, and the owner should treat
it like a password manager export. Ask before including memory; default to including it
only after they say yes. Never make the repo public, never add collaborators on your own.

## 3. Build the repo

1. Pick a working folder on the box, e.g. `/workspace/<repo-name>/`.
2. Save the script in the appendix as `scripts/snapshot.sh`, a `.gitignore` that mirrors the
   "never back up" list, and a `README.md` describing the layout and what is excluded.
3. Export live state once (see "Live routines and memory"), then run it with no remote:
   `BACKUP_INCLUDE_MEMORY=1 bash scripts/snapshot.sh`
   (set `BACKUP_AGENTS="Name A,Name B"` to limit which bots; empty = all).
   It wipes and regenerates `agents/ skills/ connectors/ user-memory/ live/`, so deleted bots,
   routines, and skills disappear from the next snapshot.
4. Show the owner the bot list (`agents/README.md`) and the file counts. Do not paste
   memory contents into chat.

## 4. Secret scan (built into the script — don't skip it)

Before every commit the script redacts, then re-scans, for: Slack `xox?-`/`xapp-` tokens,
GitHub `ghp_`/`gho_`/`github_pat_`, GitLab `glpat-`, `sk-` keys, AWS `AKIA…`, Google `AIza…`,
PEM private keys, `Bearer <token>`, and `password=`/`password:`. Any hit left after
redaction aborts the commit; it scans the staged files a second time before committing.
If it fails, find the file, fix the source (or add an exclusion), and rerun — never weaken
the patterns to make it pass.

## 5. Push setup (repo-only token, HTTPS)

The box blocks SSH to GitHub, so use HTTPS with a token; deploy keys over SSH won't work.
1. Ask the owner to create an **empty private** repo (no README, no license) and send the
   HTTPS URL. You can't create it for them.
2. Ask for a **fine-grained personal access token**: Repository access → *Only select
   repositories* → just this repo; Permissions → *Contents: Read and write*; nothing else.
   Pick an expiry (90 days is a good default) and note the date.
3. Collect it with a **masked secret request** into an env var (default name
   `BACKUP_GIT_TOKEN`). Never ask them to paste it in chat, Slack, or email; if they do,
   tell them to revoke it and make a new one.
4. `git remote add origin https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>.git` (no token in the URL).
5. The script installs a credential helper that reads the env var at push time, so the token
   value is never written to git config, `.git-credentials`, or the repo. Verify with
   `git config --get-all credential.helper` — you should see the variable *name*, not a token.
6. Run the script again; confirm the push landed and the repo shows as private.

Other hosts: GitLab uses a project access token with `write_repository`
(`BACKUP_TOKEN_USER=oauth2`); Codeberg/Gitea use a token with repo write scope.

## 6. Nightly routine

Create one routine on this bot, at a quiet hour the owner picks (e.g. 2:30 AM local), with
wording like:

> First export live state (see "Live routines and memory" below): for each bot, write its
> routines (name, schedule, enabled, prompt) and every memory you can recall into
> `$BACKUP_LIVE_DIR` with a fresh `MANIFEST.json`. Then run
> `bash /workspace/<repo-name>/scripts/snapshot.sh`. If it exits 0 (whether it committed,
> pushed, or found no changes), stay silent — no message. If it fails, tell the owner once:
> which step failed (live export, secret scan, push auth, missing token, other), the last
> ~10 lines of output with any secret-looking text removed, and the one thing they need to
> do. Don't retry more than once, don't loosen the secret scan, don't change the remote or
> the token, and don't repeat the same failure report on later nights unless the cause changes.

## 7. Token expiry reminder

Create a one-time routine **7 days before** the token expires:

> Remind the owner the backup token expires on <date>. Steps: create a new fine-grained
> token for the same single repo with Contents read/write, then I'll collect it with a
> masked secret request into the same env var. After it's in, run the snapshot once to
> confirm the push works, then schedule the next reminder 7 days before the new expiry
> and delete this one.

## 8. Restore notes (for the README)

The repo is a reference copy, not a one-click restore. To rebuild a bot: copy its
instructions from `profile.json`, recreate routines from `agents/<bot>/live/routines.json`
(prompt + schedule), re-import skills from `skills/`, and re-add memory from
`agents/<bot>/live/memory.md` and connector instructions by hand. Secrets and connector
logins always have to be re-entered.

## Live routines and memory (required: routines and memory live server-side)

`automations/*/automation.json` and `memory/*.md` on the box are no longer the source of truth;
the script files them under `agents/<bot>/legacy-files/` only. Before running `snapshot.sh`, the
nightly backup routine must export live state with its own tools (routine status/list and
memory recall) into `$BACKUP_LIVE_DIR` (default `/workspace/bot-backup-live-export`):
`MANIFEST.json` (`exported_at` ISO 8601, per-agent status), `<agent-id>/routines.json`,
`<agent-id>/memory.md`. The script copies these to `live/` and `agents/<bot>/live/`, and refuses
to commit if the manifest is missing or older than `LIVE_MAX_AGE_H` (6h); set `REQUIRE_LIVE=0`
only for a manual one-off. A bot can usually export only its own routines and memory; mark other
bots `unavailable: <why>` in the manifest rather than guessing. Never read tokens or call internal
APIs to get this data. Restore from `agents/<bot>/live/`, not `legacy-files/`.

## Appendix: scripts/snapshot.sh

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# snapshot.sh — idempotent export of Grok Bot definitions into a private git repo.
#
# Copies bot definitions from the box (profiles, settings, live routine/memory export,
# legacy box files, user-created skills, connector custom instructions), leaves secrets and
# data out, redacts + scans for secrets (fails on any remaining hit), commits only
# when something changed, and pushes only if a remote named "origin" exists.
#
# Configuration (all optional, via environment):
#   BACKUP_DIR             repo to write into (default: the repo containing this script)
#   BACKUP_SRC             box data root (default: /home/box/agent-data)
#   BACKUP_TOKEN_VAR       NAME of the env var holding the push token (default: BACKUP_GIT_TOKEN).
#                          The token value is never written to git config or disk.
#   BACKUP_TOKEN_USER      username sent with the token (default: x-access-token, works for GitHub)
#   BACKUP_AGENTS          comma-separated bot names or agent ids to include (default: all)
#   BACKUP_INCLUDE_MEMORY  1 to export memory files, 0 to skip them (default: 1)
#   BACKUP_MAX_MB          per-file size cap in MB (default: 5)
#   BACKUP_LIVE_DIR        live export folder (default: /workspace/bot-backup-live-export)
#   LIVE_MAX_AGE_H         max age of the live export in hours (default: 6)
#   REQUIRE_LIVE           1 to fail without a fresh live export (default: 1)
#   BACKUP_GIT_NAME / BACKUP_GIT_EMAIL   commit identity (default: "Grok Bot backup" / backup@localhost)
#
# The remote is whatever `git remote get-url origin` says (set it once, HTTPS URL).
set -euo pipefail

SRC="${BACKUP_SRC:-/home/box/agent-data}"
REPO="${BACKUP_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"
TOKEN_VAR="${BACKUP_TOKEN_VAR:-BACKUP_GIT_TOKEN}"
TOKEN_USER="${BACKUP_TOKEN_USER:-x-access-token}"
INCLUDE_MEMORY="${BACKUP_INCLUDE_MEMORY:-1}"
AGENT_FILTER="${BACKUP_AGENTS:-}"
MAX_BYTES=$(( ${BACKUP_MAX_MB:-5} * 1024 * 1024 ))

for bin in git jq rg perl; do
  command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || { echo "missing required tool: $bin" >&2; exit 1; }
done
[[ "$TOKEN_VAR" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || { echo "BACKUP_TOKEN_VAR is not a valid variable name" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$SRC" ] || { echo "source not found: $SRC" >&2; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$REPO"; cd "$REPO"
[ -d .git ] || git init -q -b main
git config user.name  "${BACKUP_GIT_NAME:-Grok Bot backup}"
git config user.email "${BACKUP_GIT_EMAIL:-backup@localhost}"

# Wipe generated trees so deleted bots/skills/routines disappear from the snapshot.
rm -rf agents skills connectors user-memory live
mkdir -p agents skills connectors

SKIPPED=()
copy() { # copy <src> <dest>; skips oversized and secret-looking/transcript files
  local s="$1" d="$2" sz base
  [ -f "$s" ] || return 0
  base="$(basename "$s")"
  case "$base" in
    .env|.env.*|*.pem|*.key|*.p12|*.pfx|id_rsa*|id_ed25519*|*secret*|*token*|*credential*|*cookie*|*Cookie*|*.db|*.db-*|*.sqlite*|*.jsonl|runs.json|audit*)
      SKIPPED+=("$s (excluded type)"); return 0;;
  esac
  sz=$(stat -c %s "$s")
  if [ "$sz" -gt "$MAX_BYTES" ]; then SKIPPED+=("$s (too large)"); return 0; fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$d")"; cp -p "$s" "$d"
}
slugify() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -E 's/[^a-z0-9]+/-/g; s/^-+|-+$//g'; }
wanted() { # wanted <id> <name>: true if no filter, or id/name/slug is in BACKUP_AGENTS
  [ -z "$AGENT_FILTER" ] && return 0
  local item; IFS=',' read -ra items <<< "$AGENT_FILTER"
  for item in "${items[@]}"; do
    item="$(printf '%s' "$item" | sed -E 's/^ +| +$//g')"
    [ "$item" = "$1" ] || [ "$item" = "$2" ] || [ "$(slugify "$item")" = "$(slugify "$2")" ] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# ---- agents (discovered, never hardcoded) ----
MAP="agents/README.md"
{
  echo "# Agents"
  echo
  echo "Each folder: profile.json (name + instructions/persona), settings.json,"
  echo "group/project membership, live/ (exported routines + memory), and legacy-files/"
  echo "(old box copies of memory and automation.json; not the source of truth)."
  echo
  echo "| Folder | Name | Agent id |"
  echo "|---|---|---|"
} > "$MAP"
for dir in "$SRC"/agents/*/; do
  dir="${dir%/}"; id="$(basename "$dir")"
  [ -f "$dir/profile.json" ] || continue
  name="$(jq -r '.name // empty' "$dir/profile.json")"; [ -n "$name" ] || name="$id"
  wanted "$id" "$name" || continue
  slug="$(slugify "$name")"; [ -n "$slug" ] || slug="$id"
  [ -e "agents/$slug" ] && slug="$slug-${id:0:8}"
  out="agents/$slug"
  for f in profile.json settings.json group.json projects.json; do copy "$dir/$f" "$out/$f"; done
  for f in "$dir"/{AGENTS,INSTRUCTIONS,PERSONA,SOUL,instructions,persona}.md; do
    [ -f "$f" ] && copy "$f" "$out/$(basename "$f")"
  done
  if [ "$INCLUDE_MEMORY" = "1" ] && [ -d "$dir/memory" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r -d '' m; do copy "$m" "$out/legacy-files/memory/${m#"$dir/memory/"}"; done \
      < <(find "$dir/memory" -type f -name '*.md' -print0 | sort -z)
  fi
  for a in "$dir"/automations/*/automation.json; do
    [ -f "$a" ] || continue
    r="$(basename "$(dirname "$a")")"; copy "$a" "$out/legacy-files/automations/$r/automation.json"
  done
  echo "| \`$slug\` | $name | \`$id\` |" >> "$MAP"
done

# ---- LIVE export (server-side routines + memory) ----
# The nightly backup routine (a bot run) writes the live state with its own tools into
# $LIVE_DIR before calling this script:
#   $LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json                 {"exported_at":"<ISO8601>","exported_by":"<bot>","agents":[{"id","name","routines":N,"memory":N,"status":"ok|unavailable: <why>"}]}
#   $LIVE_DIR/<agent-id>/routines.json     [{"name","id","enabled","schedule","timezone","prompt",...}] as returned by the routine tools
#   $LIVE_DIR/<agent-id>/memory.md         every memory the bot could recall, verbatim
# Missing or stale (> LIVE_MAX_AGE_H hours) export fails the run unless REQUIRE_LIVE=0.
LIVE_DIR="${LIVE_DIR:-${BACKUP_LIVE_DIR:-/workspace/bot-backup-live-export}}"
LIVE_MAX_AGE_H="${LIVE_MAX_AGE_H:-6}"
REQUIRE_LIVE="${REQUIRE_LIVE:-1}"
live_fail() { if [ "$REQUIRE_LIVE" = "1" ]; then echo "LIVE EXPORT: $1 — refusing to snapshot stale state." >&2; exit 1; else echo "LIVE EXPORT WARNING: $1" >&2; fi; }
if [ ! -f "$LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json" ]; then
  live_fail "no $LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json"
else
  ts="$(jq -r '.exported_at // empty' "$LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json")"
  ep="$(date -d "$ts" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  age_h=$(( ( $(date +%s) - ep ) / 3600 ))
  if [ "$ep" -eq 0 ] || [ "$age_h" -ge "$LIVE_MAX_AGE_H" ]; then live_fail "manifest exported_at='$ts' is ${age_h}h old"; fi
  mkdir -p live; copy "$LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json" live/MANIFEST.json
  for d in "$LIVE_DIR"/*/; do
    [ -d "$d" ] || continue; lid="$(basename "$d")"
    slug="$(awk -F'|' -v id="\`$lid\`" '{gsub(/ /,"",$4)} $4==id {gsub(/[ `]/,"",$2); print $2}' "$MAP" | head -1)"
    [ -n "$slug" ] || slug="unknown-$lid"
    for f in routines.json memory.md; do copy "$d$f" "agents/$slug/live/$f"; done
  done
  echo "live export: $(jq -r '.exported_at' "$LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json"), agents=$(jq '.agents|length' "$LIVE_DIR/MANIFEST.json")"
fi

# ---- shared user memory (markdown only) ----
if [ "$INCLUDE_MEMORY" = "1" ] && [ -d "$SRC/user-memory" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r -d '' m; do copy "$m" "user-memory/${m#"$SRC/user-memory/"}"; done \
    < <(find "$SRC/user-memory" -type f -name '*.md' -print0 | sort -z)
fi

# ---- user-created skills (managed/plugin skills are not copied) ----
if [ -d "$SRC/workflows" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r -d '' s; do copy "$s" "skills/${s#"$SRC/workflows/"}"; done \
    < <(find "$SRC/workflows" -type f -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -path '*/.venv/*' \
          -not -path '*/venv/*' -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' -not -path '*/.git/*' -print0 | sort -z)
fi

# ---- connector custom instructions (only these keys from the box settings) ----
if [ -f "$SRC/settings.json" ]; then
  jq 'def j: if type=="string" then (try fromjson catch .) else . end;
  {
    mcpCustomInstructions:           ((.mcpCustomInstructions // {}) | j),
    mcpCustomInstructionsByServerId: ((.mcpCustomInstructionsByServerId // {}) | j),
    autoReviewInstructions:          ((.autoReviewInstructions // {}) | j)
  }' "$SRC/settings.json" > connectors/custom-instructions.json
fi

# ---- redact, then scan (fail on anything left) ----
PATTERNS=(
  'xox[abpors]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}'
  'xapp-[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}'
  'gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'
  'github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}'
  'glpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'
  '\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}'
  'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}'
  'AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}'
  'BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY'
  'Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{12,}'
  '(?i)password\s*[=:]\s*[^\s<"'\'']{3,}'
)
existing=(); for p in agents skills connectors user-memory live README.md; do [ -e "$p" ] && existing+=("$p"); done
REDACTED=0
for p in "${PATTERNS[@]}"; do
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
    P="$p" perl -0pi -e 's/$ENV{P}/[REDACTED]/g' "$f"; REDACTED=$((REDACTED+1))
    echo "redacted /$p/ in $f" >&2
  done < <(rg -l --pcre2 -e "$p" "${existing[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true)
done
args=(); for p in "${PATTERNS[@]}"; do args+=(-e "$p"); done
if rg -n --pcre2 "${args[@]}" "${existing[@]}"; then
  echo "SECRET SCAN FAILED — refusing to commit." >&2; exit 1
fi
echo "secret scan: clean (files redacted this run: $REDACTED)"

if big=$(find agents skills connectors user-memory live -type f -size +"${BACKUP_MAX_MB:-5}"M 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$big" ]; then
  echo "Oversized files found: $big" >&2; exit 1
fi
if [ ${#SKIPPED[@]} -gt 0 ]; then printf 'skipped: %s\n' "${SKIPPED[@]}"; fi

# ---- commit if changed ----
git add -A
staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)
if [ -n "$staged" ] && printf '%s\n' "$staged" | xargs -d '\n' rg -n --pcre2 "${args[@]}" --; then
  echo "SECRET SCAN FAILED on staged files." >&2; git reset -q; exit 1
fi
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "no changes; nothing to commit"
else
  git commit -q -m "snapshot $(date +%F)"
  echo "committed: $(git log -1 --format='%h %s')"
fi

# ---- push (only if origin exists) ----
if ! url=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null); then
  echo "no 'origin' remote; skipping push"; exit 0
fi
case "$url" in
  https://*) ;;
  *) echo "origin is not an HTTPS URL ($url); the box may block SSH to git hosts — use HTTPS." >&2; exit 1;;
esac
if [ -z "${!TOKEN_VAR:-}" ]; then
  echo "push token env var \$$TOKEN_VAR is empty or unset; cannot push." >&2; exit 1
fi
# Credential helper reads the token from the env var at push time; the value is never stored.
# The empty first entry clears any inherited helpers.
git config --replace-all credential.helper ''
git config --add credential.helper "!f() { echo username=$TOKEN_USER; echo \"password=\$$TOKEN_VAR\"; }; f"
git push origin HEAD
echo "pushed to origin"
```
